subject: Coldstart priming and response sculpting — follow-up

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Coldstart priming and response sculpting — follow-up

Hi Samir / Elena,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — appreciate the clarity on FinLytics' latency needs. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we get aligned on targets and the pilot scope: 

Summary of asks you shared:
- User-facing TTFT target: p95 <= 200ms for interactive flows (dashboard queries).
- Sustained peak throughput: ~450–550 RPS during batch window, steady 120–150 RPS on-demand.
- Typical request sizes: 120–200 tokens prefixed by a ~50 token context.
- Preferred streaming transport: your infra leans WebSocket but you said you're open to SSE for lower operational complexity.

Initial Redwood proposal (high level):
- Priming (coldstart warmers): run lightweight warmup on new containers after deploy to hit warm TTFT quickly; aim to reduce cold-start p95 to < 750ms for the pilot.
- Response sculpting / chunk cadence: target chunk emission every 40–80ms for interactive UX; we'll tune between 40ms (aggressive) and 120ms (conservative) in the pilot.
- Fallbacks: automatic model-fallback to a smaller-quantized variant when per-token latency exceeds thresholds; routing to a lower-cost region only if global capacity triggers.

Requested items from you to scope the pilot:
1) A week of anonymized traffic profile (RPS / burst patterns) — you can drop in the attached CSV.
2) Preference for WebSocket vs SSE for the pilot (both supported; tradeoffs below).

Attachments: slo-draft-v1.pdf (our base SLOs), finlytics-traffic-patterns.csv (please replace with your data).

Suggested next steps:
- You confirm transport choice (WS or SSE) and we’ll finalize the runbook.
- Redwood engineers (Karthik / Neha) to propose a two-week pilot with two phases: warmup tuning + chunk-cadence sweep.

Thanks — I’ll loop Ben and Karthik to drive scheduling.

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwoodinference.com

Ava — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers:
- We prefer WebSocket for the initial pilot because our edge gateway already maintains WS connections for other services and we can piggyback on that.
- Attaching a sanitized one-week traffic export (see finlytics-traffic-patterns.csv in your attachment field). Peak bursts happen in hourly batches around 09:00–10:00 PT; average session length is ~3.5 minutes.

One clarification: when you say "warmers" what is the estimated cost during a deploy window? We want to avoid significant burst charges. Also curious about the fallback behavior — will users see degraded responses or will the app degrade gracefully (e.g., shorter completions)?

Samir
Head of Platform Engineering
FinLytics
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Coldstart priming and response sculpting — follow-up

Looping in engineering to confirm feasibility and propose concrete numbers. High-level recommendation for the pilot:
- Option A (WebSocket-first): keep WS as the transport. Implement heartbeat keepalive and chunk cadence target of 60ms initially. Use incremental cadence tuning (60 -> 40ms) based on CPU/GPU headroom metrics.
- Option B (SSE fallback): run a side-by-side test where 10% of traffic uses SSE to compare latency and operational simplicity.

Pilot plan (2 weeks):
Phase 1 (3 days): traffic replay + warmup parameter sweep to get warm TTFT at p95 < 200ms for the 120–200 token size.
Phase 2 (8–11 days): cadence sweep and stability under burst. Collect per-token latency, kernel utilization, and client-observed UX metrics.

Key asks for FinLytics:
- Confirm WS is acceptable for pilot.
- Provide a single point-of-contact for scheduling (Samir / Elena).

I’ll prepare the draft runbook once engineering confirms the parameters (Neha / Karthik).

—Ben

Subject: Re: Coldstart priming and response sculpting — follow-up

Hi Samir / Elena — thanks for the file and for confirming WS preference. Quick technical note from infra on expected behavior and numbers so you can share with your SREs: 

Coldstart and warmers
- Warmers: we start 1 lightweight inference request per new worker (minimal prompt) to initialize kernels and populate KV cache. Cost: roughly 0.5–1.5s GPU time-per-worker depending on model size; we typically schedule warmers only for pre-warmed pool (can be disabled to reduce cost).
- Cold p95 goal for pilot: <= 750ms (with warmers enabled) on our tested medium-size LLM variant. Without warmers, coldstarts may spike to ~1.4–1.8s p95 depending on model loading.

TTFT / chunk cadence targets we can hit for WebSocket path
- Warm (steady) p95 TTFT target: <= 180ms at 4 concurrent requests per model shard. This assumes batching window <= 10ms and small batch sizes (1–4).
- Chunk cadence: we recommend starting at 60ms inter-chunk pacing (typical UX sweet spot). We can sweep 40/60/90ms in pilot to quantify CPU/GPU and client UX tradeoffs.

Throughput and concurrency notes
- Expected per-GPU steady throughput with our medium-quantized variant: ~1,200 tokens/s (varies by sequence length). For your 120–200 token median size, a single GPU can sustain ~200–250 requests per second with concurrency tuning.
- For your 500 RPS peak, we recommend reserving 2–3 GPUs with a 20% buffer for burst headroom during the pilot.

Fallback behavior and graceful degradation
- Fallback policy: if per-token latency breaches configured threshold for >10s, requests are routed to the fallback model (smaller quantized variant). The client receives shorter completions (we instrument with a "degraded" flag in the streaming metadata so the UI can show an explanation). No silent truncation; app-visible indicator recommended.

Runbook items we will provide before pilot start:
- Handshake + WS keepalive parameters to align with your edge gateway.
- Cadence sweep schedule and telemetry dashboard links.
- Clear rollback criteria (e.g., token p95 > 400ms sustained for 15m).

Next steps:
1) Samir / Elena confirm pilot window availability and whether we should enable warmers (suggest: yes for phase 1).
2) We will deliver a runbook and updated SLO draft (attached: slo-draft-v1.pdf) and a short test harness you can run in staging.

Happy to jump on a quick call with your SRE team if helpful.

—Neha Kapoor
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Performance | Redwood Inference
